title: Base change of proper/open interchange and open-composition factors
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $(g\prime,f\prime,f,g)$, $(a,p,f,j)$, $(c,j\prime,j,g)$, $(b,p\prime,p,c)$, $(a\prime,p\prime,f\prime,j\prime)$ and $(b,a\prime,a,g\prime)$ be Cartesian squares, with $a,j,a\prime,j\prime$ open immersions. Supply a compactification $c_f$ of $f$, put $d_f=c_f\times_Y Y\prime$, $q=c_f\times_Y U$, and $q\prime=d_f\times_{Y\prime}U\prime$. Supply $w:q\prime.Z\to q.Z$ whose open and proper factor squares are Cartesian, with $wk=k\prime z$, where $k,k\prime,z$ are the first pullback projections. Let $Q$ be the raw compactification exchange of these representatives and let $T,T\prime$ be the graph-free comparisons of [def-asd-open-support-factors]. For every complex $K$ in the unbounded etale module-derived category [def-amb-etale-compact-support], open exchange for $j$ followed by $g^*T$ and $B(c_f)$ equals $j\prime_!Q$ followed by $T\prime$ and $Rd_f{}_!$ of open exchange for $a$. This asserts coherence only for proper/open interchange and the open compositor: no arbitrary compactification of $p$ and no graph comparison occurs. There is no quasi-compactness assumption.

source.place: Coherence (i): compare the proper/open diagram with its base change; the open factors are handled by the adjunction transposition in coherence (iii).

proof.text: Apply the proper/open exchange cube to the square of cf.g against j, its base change, and the four side squares. The proper side squares are those supplied; the open side squares are sqj and the square wk=k\prime z, Cartesian by pullback cancellation. Whisker by extension along q.i.

Apply unit-normalized open exchange pasting to the two factorizations q.i;k=a;cf.i and qprime.i;kprime=aprime;df.i. Compatibility with equality of composite open morphisms identifies their outer exchange. Cancel the open compositor isomorphisms, combine with naturality of proper exchange and of proper/open interchange, and substitute into the proper/open cube. This gives the component equation for exact inverse image.

Conjugate the exact-inverse-image equation by the canonical natural isomorphisms to left derived inverse image. The explicit exchange transport equations and naturality cancel the endpoint comparison isomorphisms, yielding the displayed equation for the supplied derived exchanges.
